newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV REACHES QUARTERS IN NEW HAVEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV REACHES QUARTERS IN NEW HAVEN.

text.p: Top-seeded Yevgeny Kavelnikov easily gained the quarter-finals of the Pilot Pen tennis tournament Thursday, while American David Wheaton produced the big surprise with a three-set upset of third-seeded Australian Marc Philippoussis.
Kafelnikov, a Russian ranked sixth in the world, needed only 56 minutes to defeat Slava Dosedel of the Czech Republic 6-2 6-3 at the Connecticut Tennis Center.
"My game plan is simple, I just try to hit as many balls as I can," said the 23-year-old former French Open champion.
"I feel pretty confident right now and I'm saving my energy for the last."
In Friday's quarter-finals, Kafelnikov will face seventh-seeded Tim Henman of Britain, a 6-4 6-4 winner over Brett Steven of New Zealand.
Wheaton stunned Philippoussis 6-7 (2-7) 6-3 6-4 in the second round, and he followed with a 7-6 (8-6) 6-4 victory over Germany's Marc Goellner to gain the quarter-finals.

Wheaton, playing his big serve-and-volley game, recovered effectively after losing the tiebreaker against Philippoussis. Philippoussis, known for one of the hardest serves in the game, enjoyed a narrow 11-9 edge in aces but Wheaton made a higher percentage of first serves and broke his opponent's service five times.
At 4-4 in the third set, Wheaton took the last two games at love. "I lost eight points on unforced effors and that's all it takes," said Philippoussis.

Wheaton, who was out of action for seven months due to foot surgery, saw his ranking sink to 142 going into this tournament. "This was a great day for me...very satisfying," he said. "I was eager to play."
Second-seeded Sergi Bruguera of Spain, yet to lose a set in this tournament, gained a 6-4 7-6 (7-4) decision over countryman Francisco Clavet.
Fourth seed Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands, fifth seed Petr Korda of the Czech Republic and 11th seed Greg Rusedski of Britain also moved into the round of eight with straight-set victories.
Krajicek beat Kenneth Carlsen of Denmark 7-6 (7-1) 6-2, Korda defeated Javier Sanchez of Spain 6-2 6-4 and Rusedski upset sixth-seeded Albert Costa of Spain 6-3 7-6 (7-5).
American Alex O'Brien, seeded only 14th although he was the defending champion, was eliminated by Marc-Kevin Goellner of Germany 7-5 6-3.
"I played very poorly," O'Brien said. "I felt a little slow and lethargic. Maybe I should use my brain a little more."
He added: "Goellner played a very good match. He really took it to me. I had beaten him the last two times and he wanted some revenge."
Eighth-seeded Patrick Rafter of Australia survived a two-hour battle with Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev 6-3 2-6 6-4.
